meta.subtitle: How the kit fits together at runtime. Useful when something doesn't behave as expected, or when you want to extend a primitive.

blocks.summary: JSON pages are walked by renderer.js at load time and turned into Custom-Element DOM. chrome.js owns the behavior of those Custom Elements plus the page-level chrome (TOC, search, theme, warnings, viewport tracking). The whole kit lives in three JS files + one CSS file + JSON registry files.
bullets: Format: JSON tree → renderer.js walks it → Custom Element DOM → chrome.js attaches behavior.
kit.json + per-domain glossary/extref JSON files are the registry; loaded once at page start, resolved per element.
Visual Viewport API keeps fixed-position chrome buttons anchored during pinch-zoom on Safari.
Build pipeline (html-doc CLI) produces 4 artifacts: site-manifest.json, llms.txt, dist/site/, dist/standalone/.

blocks.title: Files in the kit
blocks.lead: The kit repo contains all the runtime plus the registry data plus the CLI.

blocks.source:
html-doc/
├── bin/html-doc                  # Python CLI — init, build, serve
├── src/html_doc/                 # CLI implementation
│   └── templates/                # starter page pair for `html-doc init`
├── src/html_doc_tests/           # pytest suite
├── kit/                          # chrome.{js,css}, chrome-boot.js, renderer.js,
│                                 # schema/, glossary/, extrefs/
├── docs/                         # this site — JSON-only sources + _kit symlink
├── examples/                     # tour pages — same shape as docs/
└── README.md, CLAUDE.md

content: chrome.js is ~4.5k lines in one file. Splitting it would mean either more script tags in every stub (worse onboarding) or a build step (more complexity, defeating the no-build-for-content goal). The current bet: one file with a clear table of contents at the top (see the section banner there). Reviewed each time the design changes shape; still wins on author ergonomics.

blocks.title: Runtime — when a page loads
blocks.lead: From the moment the browser receives the HTML stub to the moment the page is interactive.

blocks.caption: Lifecycle of a page load.
blocks.source:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant B as Browser
    participant H as HTML stub
    participant Boot as chrome-boot.js
    participant C as chrome.js
    participant R as renderer.js
    participant K as kit.json + glossary/*

    B->>H: GET page.html
    H-->>B: 1KB stub
    B->>Boot: synchronous — set data-theme pre-paint
    Note over B: paint cover + chrome buttons (no FOUC)
    B->>C: defer-load chrome.js
    B->>R: defer-load renderer.js
    C->>K: fetch kit.json (DOMContentLoaded)
    K-->>C: domains, lang, overrides
    C->>K: fetch glossary/<domain>.json (parallel)
    K-->>C: domain entries
    H->>R: autoBoot()
    R->>B: fetch page.json
    B-->>R: page tree
    R->>B: emit Custom Element DOM
    R->>C: dispatch html-doc:rendered
    C->>B: build TOC + init reading aids
    B->>C: each <glossary-term>.connectedCallback resolves data-def
    Note over B: tooltips ready, search button visible

blocks.title: The renderer
blocks.lead: renderer.js is a tree walker. It maps each JSON node's kind to a Custom Element instantiation (for interactive primitives) or directly to a styled DOM subtree (for prose primitives). The renderer is ~500 lines of straightforward code.

items: — sets document.title, picks up accent override, renders cover, walks blocks.
— switch on kind; each kind has a small _renderX function.
— walks paragraph.content arrays mixing strings (textContent) with inline nodes (createElement).

For complex primitives (chart, diagram, snippet), the renderer creates the Custom Element with attributes and a JSON-payload script child. The Custom Element's connectedCallback parses the payload and renders its own DOM.

blocks.title: Why JSON-payload-as-script-child for complex primitives
blocks.content: Attribute values can't safely encode multi-line strings or nested objects. A child <script type="application/json"> sidesteps the encoding problem entirely — the Custom Element does JSON.parse on its textContent.

blocks.title: Tooltip controller
blocks.lead: Single global controller, attached to both glossary-term and ext-ref elements. ~150 lines.

steps.title: Hover detection
steps.content: matchMedia('(hover: none)') gates the hover path — touch devices skip it and use click only. Re-evaluated per attach so input-mode changes mid-session take effect on later elements.

steps.title: Show with delay
steps.content: 120ms delay on mouseenter before showing — prevents flicker when brushing past.

steps.title: Bridge-hover
steps.content: On mouseleave, start a 300ms hide timer. If the mouse enters the tooltip DOM during that window, the timer cancels — the tooltip stays so the user can select text or click links.

steps.title: Click to pin
steps.content: Clicking the term pins the tooltip — it stays open until clicked again or another term is opened. Visible 2px accent ring marks pinned.

steps.title: Click outside / Esc
steps.content: Click anywhere outside .gloss or .tooltip-popup unpins. Escape key also unpins. Touch devices have click-only — no hover path, so click toggles pinned.

blocks.title: Visual Viewport API — pinch-zoom
blocks.lead: Fixed-position chrome anchored to the user-visible viewport rather than the layout viewport. Without this, pinch-zoom on Safari moves the visual viewport and the chrome buttons drift off-screen.

content: Two CSS variables, one event handler.
optional chaining gates the whole thing on Visual Viewport API support — graceful degrade on browsers without it (buttons stay at layout-viewport corners, same as v1).

blocks.title: kit.json + glossary loader
blocks.lead: Loads kit.json (project config) and per-domain glossary/extref files. Promise-based; returns a promise that resolves to the populated kit when all fetches complete.

steps.title: Defer
steps.content: Initial load deferred to DOMContentLoaded — gives the standalone build a chance to inline the kit bundle before fetch tries to run.

steps.title: Standalone check
steps.content: If the page has an inline __htmldoc_kit_bundle__ script (set by build_standalone), hydrate from it synchronously and skip all fetches.

steps.title: Standalone-but-no-bundle
steps.content: If __htmldoc_page__ is present but no bundle (i.e., handwritten standalone), resolve with an empty kit — tooltips degrade to plain text rather than showing 'Unknown term' for everything.

steps.title: Dev / dist/site/ path
steps.content: Fetch kit.json + each domain's glossary/extref file in parallel. After Promise.all resolves, apply project-local overrides on top. Then resolve and unblock any waiters.

blocks.title: Docs-root discovery
blocks.lead: kit.json and site-manifest.json live at the project root, not the page directory. The kit needs to find the root from any page depth.

content: gives us a URL with the docs root as its prefix — strip everything from
All kit.json, site-manifest.json, glossary/*.json, and pagefind/ fetches use this base, so subfolder pages work without per-page configuration.

blocks.title: Build pipeline
blocks.lead: bin/html-doc build walks the project, produces four output artifacts. Soft-fails on optional dependencies (Pagefind, jsonschema) so the kit doesn't acquire hard requirements.

blocks.caption: Build inputs and outputs.
blocks.source:
flowchart LR
    subgraph IN[Project source]
      P[*.json pages]
      H[*.html stubs]
      KJ[kit.json]
    end
    subgraph K[Kit — symlinked _kit/]
      KIT[chrome.css/js, renderer.js]
      G[glossary/*.json]
      E[extrefs/*.json]
    end
    BUILD[html-doc build]
    P --> BUILD
    H --> BUILD
    KJ --> BUILD
    G --> BUILD
    E --> BUILD
    KIT --> BUILD
    BUILD --> M[site-manifest.json]
    BUILD --> L[llms.txt]
    BUILD --> S[dist/site/]
    BUILD --> D[dist/standalone/]
    BUILD --> PF[dist/site/pagefind/]
    PF -.-> |if pagefind on PATH| BUILD

items: walk the project recursively for JSON pages with
write site-manifest.json with one entry per page (path, title, parent, order, summary).
write llms.txt with one Markdown link per page — for AI consumers.
if jsonschema is installed, validate every page against schema/page.schema.json; print errors with field paths.

build_site: copy every HTML stub + sibling JSON into dist/site/<rel-path>; copy _kit/ as dist/site/_kit/ for self-contained deployable; embed extracted text via hidden data-pagefind-body div for indexing.
build_standalone: for each page, inline chrome.css + chrome.js + renderer.js + page JSON + kit bundle into a single self-contained file.
if pagefind is on PATH, index dist/site/ to dist/site/pagefind/.

blocks.title: Standalone kit bundle
blocks.lead: build_standalone embeds the project's kit.json + active domain glossary + extref entries as one JSON script tag. The kit loader hydrates from it synchronously when present.

blocks.source:
<!-- dist/standalone/page.html — near the closing </body> -->
<script type="application/json" id="__htmldoc_page__">{ ... page tree ... }</script>
<script type="application/json" id="__htmldoc_kit_bundle__">{
  "kit": { "domains": ["data-platforms", ...], "lang": "en", ... },
  "glossary": { "data-platforms": { "ACID": { ... } }, ... },
  "extrefs":  { "data-platforms": { ... }, ... }
}</script>

blocks.title: Result — single-file offline tooltips
blocks.content: A single HTML file you can email or archive. All Custom Elements work, tooltips resolve, the page renders. Network requirements: Google Fonts (graceful fallback if blocked) and Mermaid CDN (only if the page has a <diagram>). Everything else inlined.
Five behaviors worth knowing about if you're reading the kit code.

blocks.title: Kit assets resolver
blocks.content: Two valid asset layouts now: development (chrome.{css,js} at repo root) and installed (chrome.{css,js} inside html_doc/assets/ in the wheel). cli._kit_assets_dir() picks whichever exists, so html-doc init works from a clone OR from uv tool install .. Hatchling force-include in pyproject packs the assets into the right place at wheel build time.

blocks.title: Generated files at the docs root, not the project root
blocks.content: cmd_serve writes site-manifest.json, site-manifest.js, llms.txt, and page.md twins at the closest common parent of JSON pages — typically docs/. _common_docs_dir(root, pages) in cli.py picks the directory, so the manifest URL prefix matches the served tree and git status stays clean.

blocks.title: Serve-time Pagefind
blocks.content: cmd_serve spawns a background thread at startup that builds dist/_search/site/ (just like cmd_build) and runs pagefind against it. Symlinks <docs-dir>/pagefind → that index so chrome.js's existing search-loader path resolves. Soft-fails if pagefind isn't installed. Opt out with --no-search.

blocks.title: Boot stamp
blocks.content: chrome.js console.info()s [html-doc] kit boot · build=<date> · docsRoot=… · authToken=yes/no at startup. Bump __htmldocKitBuild whenever a compatibility-affecting change ships so a stale-cache user can confirm from DevTools whether their browser is on the right chrome.js.

blocks.title: IntelliJ _ijt token propagation
blocks.content: chrome-boot.js plucks _ijt from window.location.search and exposes window.__htmldocWithAuth(url) that appends it to internal asset URLs (same-origin only — CDN URLs stay untouched). chrome.js and renderer.js wrap every fetch and script-src load through it so IntelliJ's built-in server stops 404'ing sub-resource requests.
